Run edgeR-QLF Differential Accessibility (DA) Analysis on Pseudobulk Data (Libra Engine)

Source: R/05_metrics_de_signal.R
run_edger_qlf_da.Rd

Performs differential accessibility (DA) analysis for scATAC-seq or differential expression (DE) for scRNA-seq on replicate pseudobulk count matrices using edgeR's Quasi-Likelihood F-test (QLF) model (Squair et al., Nature Communications 2021; Teo et al., Nature Communications 2024 / Libra).

Usage

run_edger_qlf_da(
  pseudobulk_mat,
  groups,
  fdr_cutoff = 0.05,
  logfc_cutoff = 0,
  norm_method = c("TMM", "RLE", "none")
)

Arguments

pseudobulk_mat

Pseudobulk count matrix (features/peaks x sample_replicates).

groups

Factor or character vector of comparison group conditions for each column in pseudobulk_mat.

fdr_cutoff

Adjusted p-value significance threshold (default 0.05).

logfc_cutoff

Absolute log2 fold-change threshold (default 0).

norm_method

Normalization method for edgeR calcNormFactors: "TMM" (default), "RLE", or "none".

Value

A data.frame of differential accessibility results:

feature

Peak/gene identifier

logFC

log2 fold change between conditions

logCPM

Average log2 counts per million

F_stat

Quasi-likelihood F-statistic

PValue

Raw p-value from F-test

FDR

Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value

is_da

Logical flag indicating whether the region is significantly differentially accessible

Details

Fits negative binomial generalized linear models using Empirical Bayes quasi-likelihood dispersion shrinkage and F-tests (`edgeR::glmQLFit` and `edgeR::glmQLFTest`), offering benchmark-proven control over false discovery rates across biological replicates.

Examples

mat <- matrix(rpois(100 * 4, lambda = 10), nrow = 100, ncol = 4)
rownames(mat) <- paste0("Peak_", 1:100)
colnames(mat) <- c("Rep1:A", "Rep2:A", "Rep1:B", "Rep2:B")
groups <- c("A", "A", "B", "B")
res <- run_edger_qlf_da(mat, groups)
head(res)
#>        feature      logFC   logCPM    F_stat     PValue       FDR is_da
#> Peak_1  Peak_1 -0.2606915 13.79811 0.5929909 0.44594805 0.9000085 FALSE
#> Peak_2  Peak_2 -0.1231070 13.22553 0.0524159 0.82011968 0.9000085 FALSE
#> Peak_3  Peak_3 -0.3490234 13.39955 0.5677554 0.45572100 0.9000085 FALSE
#> Peak_4  Peak_4  0.4471192 13.39955 0.9394291 0.33845539 0.9000085 FALSE
#> Peak_5  Peak_5 -0.7985621 13.46369 3.2861166 0.07764638 0.8013723 FALSE
#> Peak_6  Peak_6 -0.6912661 13.64058 3.0323557 0.08957894 0.8013723 FALSE
